Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-prompt-long-0180", "row_sha256": "81691347498e0c232349f06f1aba6832c571a471af83c715d5b7ddbf2de52277", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
hi, can you turn all this into a clear request for a camera repair estimate, not the estimate itself. this is for Eli Navarro and the camera is a Fujifilm X-T5, serial number 4XT5-781204, received by Northline Camera Service on 14 May. Mara Ives did the bench inspection on 16 May. Keep the estimate limited to the camera body. Eli also dropped off a Fujinon XF 16–80mm lens, but that lens was only left for storage while the body is being checked; nobody inspected it, and it must not be included as an item to repair or diagnose.

Eli reported that the camera slipped from a low table onto a tile floor on 11 May. It landed on its bottom-right corner, with the 23mm lens attached. He said it powered on afterwards, but the rear screen went black once and the camera shut down twice during the next hour. He did not see a warning message. The body was not exposed to rain or liquid, according to Eli, and he has not tried to open it. The attached lens had no visible damage when it was dropped off, but that isn't an inspection result. Please keep what Eli reported separate from what Mara observed. Don't turn the incident into a confirmed cause of any fault.

Mara's written notes say the bottom-right corner has a shallow dent, the battery door closes, and the exterior shows no cracks. The battery inserted at the bench read 62 percent before testing. Mara used that same battery for the checks; there was no second battery available. The camera powered on three times during a 20-minute bench check. On two attempts the rear screen displayed the menu normally. On the third attempt it stayed black for about 40 seconds while the top status display remained lit, then the rear screen returned after Mara pressed the playback button. Mara wrote, “screen delay observed once; cause not determined.” Keep that quotation word for word.

The viewfinder displayed an image during all three power-on checks. The shutter fired five times in single-frame mode, and five files appeared on the test SD card. Mara did not test continuous shooting, video recording, wireless functions, or the camera with a different lens. The test card was Northline's card, not Eli's. Mara did not remove the outer covers or inspect internal connectors. No error code appeared during those bench checks. Eli said he had seen no error code at home either, but that is his report rather than a bench finding. Don't suggest that the camera has passed a full functional test.

There is a small gap at the right edge of the bottom plate near the dent. Mara could slide a paper strip into the gap a few millimeters, but she didn't measure it with a gauge. She did not see loose material or a bent screw head. She couldn't tell from the external check whether the frame, a connector, or a display component had shifted. Keep that uncertainty. Don't state that there is internal damage, and don't say there is none. The body has not been cleaned, adjusted, repaired, or disassembled so far. Eli asked whether it is safe to keep using it; the notes don't answer that, so include it as a question needing a technician's assessment, not a safety conclusion.

For the estimate, ask the service desk to give separate prices for further diagnosis and for any repair it can support from the findings. There are no labor rates, parts prices, tax figures, turnaround times, or parts-availability details in the notes. Don't invent numbers or promise a schedule. If a price or timing detail is unavailable until the camera is opened or a part is identified, mark it as pending and explain what would establish it. Eli wants to know whether the exterior dent can be left alone if it is cosmetic, but the notes don't establish that it is only cosmetic. He also wants to know whether the intermittent screen behavior might be related to the impact; keep that as an open question, not a diagnosis.

please make the finished estimate easy to scan and keep the reported history distinct from inspection evidence. Put the inspection evidence before any recommendation. Then give the proposed actions in a numbered checklist, with each separately priced option shown as its own item if the service desk can price it. The checklist should let Eli accept or decline each proposed item individually; don't bundle uncertain work into an approved repair. Identify which points are confirmed observations, which come from Eli, and which still need checking. If further diagnosis is needed before repair can be priced, say so without pretending a diagnosis has already happened.

1. Start with the customer and camera details, receipt date, and the limit that this estimate concerns the body only.
2. Summarize Eli's drop description and symptoms as reported history, not verified causes.
3. Present Mara's bench findings, tests, and test limits before recommendations.
4. Use a numbered checklist for diagnostic or repair options and make individual approval possible for each item.
5. Show costs and timing only when supported by the supplied notes; otherwise identify what is pending.

Eli's main concern is whether the camera is dependable enough for a family graduation on 2 June. That's why he's asking for an estimate now, but it isn't a request for Northline to guarantee performance by that date. His message says, “I can bring my own battery and card back if that helps, but please call before opening the body.” Keep both parts of that request. In particular, further tests with Eli's battery or card can be listed as questions or possible diagnostic steps, but do not imply he has already brought them in or that they have been tested. Please organize this into a realistic prompt asking for an estimate based only on the material above. The last paragraph of the estimate request should retain the graduation date, the absence of a performance guarantee, and Eli's quoted instruction to call before opening the body. Don't add a final recommendation or claim that Eli has approved any work.", "output": "Prepare a clear, easy-to-scan camera repair estimate for Eli Navarro based only on the information below. Do not treat this request as authorization to perform work. Keep the estimate limited to the Fujifilm X-T5 camera body; the accompanying Fujinon XF 16–80mm lens was left for storage, was not inspected, and must not be included for repair or diagnosis.

## Customer and equipment
- Customer: Eli Navarro
- Camera: Fujifilm X-T5
- Serial number: 4XT5-781204
- Received by Northline Camera Service: 14 May
- Bench inspection by Mara Ives: 16 May

## Reported history
Eli reported that the camera slipped from a low table onto a tile floor on 11 May, landing on its bottom-right corner with a 23mm lens attached. He said the camera powered on afterward, but its rear screen went black once and it shut down twice during the following hour. He saw no warning message. Eli reported no exposure to rain or liquid and said he has not tried to open the camera. He also said he saw no error code at home. Keep these statements clearly identified as customer-reported history, not bench findings or confirmed causes. The attached lens had no visible damage when dropped off, but it was not inspected.

## Inspection evidence and limits
Mara's notes record a shallow dent at the bottom-right corner, a closing battery door, and no exterior cracks. The battery used at the bench read 62 percent before testing; it was the only battery available. During a 20-minute bench check, the camera powered on three times. The rear screen displayed the menu on two attempts. On the third, it remained black for about 40 seconds while the top status display stayed lit, then returned after Mara pressed the playback button. Preserve Mara's note exactly: “screen delay observed once; cause not determined.”

The viewfinder displayed an image in all three checks. The shutter fired five times in single-frame mode, and five files appeared on Northline's test SD card. Continuous shooting, video recording, wireless functions, and operation with a different lens were not tested. Eli's card was not used. Mara did not remove the outer covers or inspect internal connectors. No error code appeared during the bench checks. Do not describe these limited checks as a full functional test or state that the camera passed one.

Mara noted a small gap at the right edge of the bottom plate near the dent. A paper strip entered the gap a few millimeters; no gauge measurement was taken. She saw no loose material or bent screw head. The external check did not establish whether the frame, a connector, or a display component had shifted. The camera has not been cleaned, adjusted, repaired, or disassembled. Do not assert that internal damage is present or absent. Eli asked whether it is safe to continue using the camera; the notes do not answer that. Present it as a question for a technician to assess, not as a safety conclusion.

## Requested estimate and approvals
Put the inspection evidence before recommendations. Then use a numbered checklist for proposed diagnostic or repair actions. Show each separately priced option as its own item when the service desk can price it, so Eli can accept or decline each item individually. Do not bundle uncertain work into an approved repair, and do not imply that Eli has approved any work.

Ask the service desk to provide separate prices for further diagnosis and for any repair supported by the findings. The supplied notes contain no labor rates, parts prices, tax figures, turnaround times, or parts-availability details. Do not invent costs or promise a schedule. If pricing or timing depends on opening the body or identifying a part, mark it as pending and explain what would establish it. If further diagnosis is needed before a repair can be priced, say so without presenting a diagnosis as already completed.

Eli wants to know whether the dent can be left alone if it is cosmetic, but the notes do not establish that it is only cosmetic. He also asked whether the intermittent screen behavior might be related to the impact. Keep both as open questions, not conclusions. Further tests with Eli's battery or card may be listed as questions or possible diagnostic steps, but do not imply that either has been supplied or tested.

Eli's main concern is whether the camera will be dependable enough for a family graduation on 2 June. This is his reason for requesting an estimate now, not a request for Northline to guarantee performance by that date. His message says, “I can bring my own battery and card back if that helps, but please call before opening the body.” Retain both parts of his request. In particular, the final paragraph of the estimate request must retain the graduation date, the absence of a performance guarantee, and Eli's quoted instruction to call before opening the body. Do not add a final recommendation."}]
